item.title: Denominators of Hodge integrals and Minkowski numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.30274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals is the Minkowski number $T_{2g}$ or, equivalently, the Bhargava factorial $(2g+1)!_{\mathbb{P}}$ associated to the set of primes $\mathbb{P}\subset\mathbb{N}$. As a corollary, we prove a conjecture of Liu-Xu on the multiplicity of $3$ in the least common denominators of certain descendant integrals, and generalise their result on a conjecture of Itzykson-Zuber to Hodge integrals with $\lambda$ classes. Namely, the order of the automorphism group of any pointed stable curve of genus $g'\le g$ divides the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals. We also comment on the use of generative AI via IMProofBench, which played a fruitful part in the development of this (entirely human-written) paper.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Holmes

item.title: Relative Hitchin fibrations and endoscopy for Unitary Friedberg--Jacquet varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.30366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a relative fundamental lemma for the unitary symmetric variety $GL_n(k')\backslash U_{2n}$, proving a conjecture of Leslie, Xiao, and Zhang. Our proof reduces to the Lie algebra and argues over function fields in positive characteristic, using methods from Ngo-Laumon and Ngo. In particular, we reinterpret orbital integrals in terms of the cohomology of relative affine Springer fibers and globalize this using unitary versions of Hitchin moduli spaces for symmetric pairs via a product formula. As the main global input, we prove a matching of perverse sheaves between relative Hitchin moduli spaces and their corresponding endoscopic variants.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hameister, Spencer Leslie

item.title: Asymptotics of local height pairing without Hodge conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.30574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We remove the assumption of the Hodge conjecture from the asymptotic formula for the Archimedean local height established in our previous work. We also remove other minor assumptions. We achieve this by exploiting the cohomological nature of Beilinson's local intersection index rather than arguing motivically.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Nakayama

item.title: The dual complex and RC-invariant functors
item.description: arXiv:2610.30608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the dual complex of a simple normal crossings divisor to a homotopy type invariant $\mathcal{D}(X)$ of arbitrary complex varieties, and we prove that it is contractible when $X$ is connected and of klt type. In fact, the dual complex belongs to a broader class of invariants, which we call RC (rationally connected)-invariant functors. We prove a rigidity theorem governing the behavior of such functors with respect to rationally connected fibrations.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Burke

item.title: Obstructions to deforming space curves lying on a complete intersection of quadrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.30962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S=S_{2,\ldots,2}\subset\mathbb P^{n+2}$ be a smooth complete intersection of $n$ quadrics containing a line $E$, where $n\geq 3$, and set $D=(n-1)\mathbf h+E$, where $\mathbf h=[\mathcal O_S(1)]$. We study the deformations of smooth curves $C\in |mD|$ and their obstructions. The linear system $|D|$ defines a birational morphism $f:S\to\overline S$ that contracts $E$ to a point and realizes an unprojection in the sense of Papadakis--Reid. When $n=3$, the surface $S=S_{2,2,2}\subset\mathbb P^5$ is a $K3$ surface and $E$ is a $(-2)$-curve. We prove that the complementary open surface $S\setminus E$ admits first-order infinitesimal deformations in $\mathbb P^5\setminus E$ that are obstructed at the second order. Using these obstructions, we show that, for every sufficiently large $m$ with $\operatorname{char} k\nmid m$, there exists a generically non-reduced irreducible component $W_m$ of the Hilbert scheme $\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^5$ of smooth connected curves in $\mathbb P^5$. Its general member $C$ lies on a complete intersection $S_{2,2,2}$ of three quadrics, satisfies $C\sim mD$, and has $h^0(N_{C/\mathbb P^5})-\dim_{[C]}\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^5=3$. In contrast, when $n>3$, we prove that, for every sufficiently large $m$ with $\operatorname{char} k\nmid m$, the corresponding family of curves in $|mD|$ gives rise to a generically smooth irreducible component of $\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^{n+2}$.
item.dc:creator: Hirokazu Nasu

item.title: Uniformity of the minimal exponent on the GIT boundary of projective hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.30985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a non-stable (in the sense of GIT) hypersurface of degree $d \ge 3$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{n}$. S. G. Park proved that the global minimal exponent of $X$ satisfies the inequality $\widetilde{\alpha}(X) \le \frac{n+1}{d}$. In this paper, we establish the uniform sharpness of this inequality: we prove that $\widetilde{\alpha}(X) = \frac{n+1}{d}$ holds for a general member $X$ of every irreducible component of the strictly semistable locus. Moreover, a general point of each irreducible component of the GIT boundary $\partial M^{\mathrm{GIT}}$ admits a strictly semistable zero-weight representative with this minimal exponent. By the lower semicontinuity of the minimal exponent on the affine cone and a theorem of Musta\c{t}\u{a}--Popa for general linear combinations of monomials, the problem is reduced to computing the log canonical thresholds, at the cone vertex, of the monomial ideals associated with the maximal strictly semistable supports with respect to a maximal torus and their weight-zero parts. Since the barycenter of the degree-$d$ simplex lies in the convex hull of each of these supports, Howald's formula forces these thresholds to be uniformly equal to $\frac{n+1}{d}$.
item.dc:creator: Yasutaka Shibata

item.title: Third-Order Weierstrass Points on Plane Quartics
item.description: arXiv:2610.30992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a smooth plane quartic $C$, the $3$-Weierstrass points are the $300$ points (counted with weights) at which some plane cubic has contact order at least ten with $C$. Revisiting the work of Kamel and Elshareef, we write the third Veronese Wronskian as an $\text{SL}_3$-covariant form $\Omega_3$ of degree $75$, given by a determinant of iterated Hamiltonian derivatives, and explain the special $3$-Weierstrass points through contact cubics and homologies preserving $C$. We determine $\Omega_3$ for the Fermat, Komiya--Kuribayashi, Klein and Picard quartics; for the Klein quartic $\Omega_3\equiv\Phi_6^2\,\Phi_{21}\,(3\Phi_{14}^3+21962\,\Phi_6^7)$ modulo the curve, up to a non-zero scalar. Finally, the dectactic points of the Fermat quartic are not $4$-Weierstrass points, which disproves a conjecture of Kamel and Elshareef. All computations are supported by \texttt{SINGULAR} scripts.
item.dc:creator: Ewelina Nawara

item.title: The classification of smooth 3-fold flops
item.description: arXiv:2610.31073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes the analytic classification of smooth, simple, 3-fold flops, and in the process provides both an intrinsic characterisation and a classification of their contraction algebras.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Brown, Michael Wemyss

item.title: The taming of 3-fold flops
item.description: arXiv:2610.31079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article overviews recent progress in understanding and classifying one of the most elementary of birational surgeries within algebraic geometry, namely 3-fold flops, through the development of a noncommutative version of singularity theory.
item.dc:creator: Michael Wemyss

item.title: Gamma conjectures for Milnor hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Gamma conjectures I and II of Galkin, Golyshev and Iritani for Milnor hypersurfaces, the smooth hypersurfaces of bidegree $(1,1)$ in the product of two projective spaces. We provide a criterion for Gamma conjecture II for general Fano manifolds, generalizing the criterion by Hu and Ke. Using the mirror symmetry technique of Galkin and Iritani, we establish global Gamma-I for Milnor hypersurfaces, thereby proving Gamma conjecture I as a special case. Using it, together with the Galois action and our criterion, we verify Gamma conjecture II for Milnor hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jianxun Hu, Hua-Zhong Ke, Changzheng Li, Jiayu Song

item.title: Positivity of supercritical LYZ pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the roots of supercritical Leung--Yau--Zaslow pairs and prove pointwise strong positivity of the associated Schur forms. The resulting LYZ cones contain the pliant cone on smooth projective threefolds, with strict inclusion on a Fujino--Sato threefold. We also establish Hard Lefschetz and Hodge--Riemann relations for the associated Chern classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds in bidegrees $1\le p+q\le\dim X$ with $\min\{p,q\}\le1$.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Liu, Mao Sheng, Shing-Tung Yau

item.title: Three-dimensional noncommutative Fano minifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.31250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a construction of the previously announced family of three-dimensional noncommutative Fano minifolds of Euler degree $72$. We prove that their defining $\mathbb{Z}$-algebras are Koszul and Artin--Schelter regular, and compute the Hilbert series of their section algebras.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Loginov, Dmitri Orlov

item.title: Log blow-ups and global resolutions in rigid geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.31265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we study log blow-ups in the setting of log adic spaces. As in the theory of log schemes, we prove the existence of global resolutions of toric singularities for fs log adic spaces log smooth over a $p$-adic field, and the acyclicity of certain sheaves under log blow-ups. One new feature of (log) rigid analytic varieties is their integral structure sheaf: we prove that it is also almost acyclic under log blow-ups in the Kummer \'etale topology. We also supply some foundational results on log adic spaces.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Shao

item.title: Cohomology of integral structure sheaves for open varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.31289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the cohomology of integral structure sheaves for two types of open rigid analytic varieties: complements of divisors in quasi-compact varieties, and partially proper spaces. As applications, we prove a strengthened form of the Hebbarkeitssatz (Riemann's extension theorem), involving the almost vanishing of $R^1\lim$, and study pro-\'etale $G$-torsors on open varieties.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Shao

item.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
item.description: arXiv:2610.31379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and let $V$ be a four-dimensional symplectic $K$-vector space. We study the Penrose incidence correspondence $\mathbb{P}(V) \leftarrow \mathrm{Flag}(1,2;V) \rightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ after Berkovich analytification. The Klein quadric $\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ decomposes into the open orbit $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ and the Lagrangian quadric, which parametrize respectively the projective lines transverse and tangent to the standard contact distribution on $\mathbb{P}(V)$. We construct explicit free discrete subgroups $\Gamma\subset\mathrm{PSp}(V)$ and analytic domains, cut out by Drinfeld upper half-spaces, in all three members of the incidence diagram. Both incidence projections are surjective on these domains, the three $\Gamma$-actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the Penrose double correspondence descends to the analytic quotients. The quotient of the twistor domain is a contact analytic threefold, and the Grassmannian domain is contained in the analytification of the $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ open orbit.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Verjovsky

item.title: An asymptotic $\Gamma$-BMT inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.31399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We refine a bound of Cheng-Feyzbakhsh to prove an asymptotic $\Gamma$-Bayer-Macr\`i-Toda ($\Gamma$-BMT) inequality on every smooth polarized complex threefold. The proof relies on a reduction to small tilt stability parameters. Using this inequality we verify Feyzbakhsh-Thomas's condition $(wBG)$ whenever $K_{X}$ is numerically proportional to the polarization. For polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds, this yields a reduction of positive rank generalized Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants to those counting sheaves pure in codimension one. We further express these invariants in terms of rank one generalized DT invariants. Thus, the rank reductions of Feyzbakhsh-Thomas hold without assuming the BMT conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Nick Rekuski

item.title: Local heights for nef toric compactified divisors
item.description: arXiv:2610.31442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a definition of a local height of nef toric divisors in the sense of Yuan and Zhang by approximating a height for canonical divisors and then using the local energy to extend to other metrics on the same geometric divisor.
item.dc:creator: Clara Otte

item.title: A semiampleness result for hyperk\"ahler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.31497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a geometric proof of the following statement: let $X$ be a smooth hyperk\"ahler fourfold such that the Picard group is generated by a line bundle $L$ that is nef, non-trivial, and not big. If the Kodaira dimension of $L$ is non-negative, some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration. The proof requires a number of tools which are of independent interest, including an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing result for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.
item.dc:creator: Andreas H\"oring, Vladimir Lazi\'c, Christian Lehn

item.title: The generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most sixteen lines is combinatorial
item.description:
arXiv:2610.31556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in $\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ and let $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle$ be its bundle of logarithmic vector fields. On a general line, $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle$ splits as $\mathcal{O}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}(k+1-d)$ with $k=\min\{\mathrm{mdr}(\mathcal{A}),\lfloor rac{d-1}{2}floor\}$, where $\mathrm{mdr}$ is the minimal degree of a Jacobian syzygy. We prove that $k$ is determined by the intersection lattice whenever $d\le16$, answering in this range a question of Cook, Harbourne, Migliore and Nagel. Since freeness can be read off from $k$ and $c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle)$, this strengthens Terao's freeness conjecture in this range; in particular we obtain a proof of Terao's conjecture for $14$ lines that uses it only for $13$ lines. For any number $d$ of lines, it follows that $\mathrm{mdr}$ is determined by the lattice whenever $\mathrm{mdr}\le6$ and $2\mathrm{mdr}\le d-3$, and that Terao's conjecture holds for every free arrangement whose smaller exponent is at most $7$. The proof reduces the question to critical arrangements: $2s+3$ lines, each containing at most $s+1$ intersection points, with $\mathrm{mdr}=s$. For these, the inflection polynomial of the minimal derivation factors as $Q_\mathcal{A} R$ with $R\in H^0(\mathcal{I}_Z^2(s-3))$, where $Z$ is the zero scheme of the derivation, of length $
u=c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle)-s(s+2)$. For $s\le5$ this forces $
u\le1$, and Chern class arguments then reduce everything to Terao's conjecture for $13$ lines. For $s=6$ we show $
u\le3$, using a Riccati equation along multiple components of $R$, Ziegler's multirestriction, and local computations verified by computer algebra; an exhaustive enumeration of the 26,265,318 candidate lattices with $
u\in\{2,3\}$ that satisfy Bojanowski's inequality completes the proof.
item.dc:creator: Cristian Anghel, Rares Stan

item.title: Leafrians, Poisson structures, and Frobenius splittings on moduli spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Poisson $T$-Pfaffians of Bott--Samelson varieties, $G/U$, and $G/B$ produce Frobenius splittings, but only by a local, coordinate-bound argument. We isolate the local mechanism: a weighted trace pairing on the deformation space of a fat point, whose top coefficient factors over the blocks. At the members of a presentation, polyvector fields on the base $X$ transfer to the moduli space $M$. Applied to a Poisson bivector, this produces a Poisson bivector, extending Bottacin's structure from surfaces to arbitrary dimension. Applied to a top degree polyvector $s$ and wedged with a transverse Euler frame, it produces an anticanonical section on $M$, which we call the \emph{leafrian}. When $X$ is a Poisson surface, we prove that the leafrian splits the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons if and only if $s$ Frobenius-splits the base. The mechanism itself is dimension-free. The construction also recovers and generalizes the splittings of the Lie-theoretic examples: the $r$-matrix need not satisfy the classical Yang--Baxter equation.
item.dc:creator: Jun Peng

item.title: Almost simple subgroups of the space Cremona group
item.description: arXiv:2610.31628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every finite almost simple subgroup that is not simple of the group of birational automorphisms of the three-dimensional complex projective space is isomorphic to one of the following: $\mathfrak{S}_5$, $\mathfrak{S}_6$, $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_7)$ or $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_9)$. We also prove that the group of birational automorphisms of the three-dimensional complex projective space contains unique (up to conjugation) subgroups isomorphic to $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_7)$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_9)$.
item.dc:creator: Sebasti\'an Fuentes

item.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.30288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Niklas Garner, Martijn Kool, Jan Manschot, Yuuji Tanaka

item.title: Isogenies of Oriented Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.30376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct and describe the moduli stack $\mathrm{Isog}$ of isogenies between oriented elliptic curves. We show that $\mathrm{Isog}$ is a spectral Deligne-Mumford stack and a relative spectral algebraic space over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}^{\mathrm{or}}$, and give a fiber product decomposition of $\mathrm{Isog}$ corresponding to a connected-\'etale factorization on oriented elliptic curves. In the process of proving these results, we construct a theory of duality and quotients for spectral abelian varieties, prove a higher-algebraic version of Nakayama's lemma, and lift the rigidity theorem for morphisms of elliptic curves to the setting of spectral algebraic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Doron Grossman-Naples

item.title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
item.description: arXiv:2610.30395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.
item.dc:creator: Ruben Louis

item.title: Aspects of quadratic Chabauty via modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.30703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop algorithms to construct a basis of de Rham cohomology for modular curves and a matrix representing the Hodge filtration required in the quadratic Chabauty method. We do this without requiring an explicit plane model of the curve and instead compute these objects in terms of modular forms. Our approach works for any modular curve; to demonstrate its efficiency, we implement our method for nonsplit Cartan modular curves.
item.dc:creator: Marius Leonhardt, Isabel Rendell

item.title: Analytification and tropicalization via hyperfields and definable types
item.description: arXiv:2610.30762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the analytification and tropicalization of algebraic varieties over valued fields via Jun's spaces of hyperfield points. Our main new objects are a family of power-tropical hyperfields $H_n$ and their inverse limit $H$, recording at each level the class of a leading term modulo $n$-th powers of the residue field. They yield an enhanced tropicalization of the associated space $X(H)$, strictly finer than the Berkovich one exactly when the multiplicative group of the residue field is non-divisible: it specialises to the Berkovich analytification when the residue field is algebraically closed, to the real analytification of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu when it is real closed, and to a new $p$-adic analytification when it is $p$-adically closed. Over henselian valued fields of equicharacteristic $0$ we then construct a model-theoretic avatar of $X(H)$: the space $\widehat{X}_T$ of definable types orthogonal to the value group, which sharpens the geometry in the spirit of Hrushovski and Loeser and recovers their space over algebraically closed valued fields. We show that $\widehat{X}_T$ is strictly pro-definable, satisfies a model-theoretic Payne theorem, and definable compactness in such spaces satisfies a Heine-Borel type characterization. As an application, we analytify $p$-adic semi-algebraic sets and prove a strong density theorem for their tropicalizations, the exact $p$-adic counterpart of the real one of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Cubides Kovacsics, Mariana Vicar\'ia, Jinhe Ye

item.title: Rigidity, flexibility, and a sign error
item.description: arXiv:2610.30976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The documents [OAI26a, OAI26b, OAI26c] claimed to prove cases of the Hodge conjecture via homological mirror symmetry, before being withdrawn by OpenAI. We discuss the source of the error (but do not analyse the rest of the argument).
item.dc:creator: Yanki Lekili, Nick Sheridan

item.title: The center is the formal internal automorphism group
item.description: arXiv:2610.31411v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the deformation functor associated to an algebra over a sufficiently nice Koszul operad can be lifted to an operadic formal moduli problem over the Koszul dual operad. We further show that this operadic formal moduli problem corresponds to the derived center of the algebra under the operadic Lurie-Pridham correspondence. As an application, we prove that the classical Gerstenhaber algebra structure on polyvector fields of a commutative algebra agrees with the derived center of the algebra as an abelian Poisson algebra.
item.dc:creator: Sonja Farr

item.title: Triple Quantum Schubert Calculus
item.description: arXiv:2610.31533v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a triple quantum Pieri formula: the product of a quantum double Schubert polynomial $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)$ by a quantum factorial elementary polynomial $\widetilde{E}_{p,k}(x;z)$ in a second set of variables $z$ is a sum over chains in the quantum Bruhat graph, indexed by a quantum analogue of Sottile's relation, whose coefficients are monomials in the quantum parameters times polynomials in the differences $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and which is Graham-positive at $z=y$. At $y=z=0$ it is the quantum Pieri rule of Ciocan-Fontanine and Postnikov; at $z=y$ it is an equivariant quantum Pieri rule for the complete flag variety, indexed by chains in the quantum Bruhat graph rather than, as in the rule of Huang and Li, by the data of a reduction to classical cohomology, and proved directly. A doubled Pieri formula, positive in the same senses, treats multiplication by the quantization of a product of two elementary polynomials in the same variables, which is not the product of the quantizations: it is two iterated Pieri steps with the incompatible pairs of chains omitted. More generally, the triple quantum Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^{w,d}(y;z)$, the coefficients of $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_v(x;z)$ in the basis $\{\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_w(x;y)\}$, are polynomials in the $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients; the proof of this appears as an appendix. We extend the Peterson-Woodward comparison formula and the quantum-to-classical reduction of Leung-Li and Huang-Li to the triple constants, and we describe and prove correct the algorithms of schubmult, which compute products of arbitrary quantum double Schubert polynomials well beyond the reach of previous methods.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Samuel

item.title: Quantum K-structure constants and cylindric Grothendieck polynomials for Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2610.31607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the partition functions of a five-vertex exactly solvable lattice model from statistical mechanics to give new combinatorial formulae for the Schubert structure constants of torus-equivariant quantum K-theory rings of Grassmannians. The proofs build on our earlier results where we identified the transfer matrices of these lattice models geometrically as multiplications by the Hirzebruch $\lambda_y$ classes of the tautological subbundle and the (dual) quotient bundle. The structure constants are solutions of a system of linear equations with coefficients given by the partition function. This system may be solved explicitly by specializing the Hirzebruch parameter $y$ to an equivariant parameter, leading to explicit formulae using Cramer's rule. Furthermore, we give an alternative combinatorial construction of the partition functions in terms of sums over cylindric set-valued tableaux, which we call cylindric Grothendieck polynomials. The latter generalise McNamara's factorial skew Grothendieck and Yeliussizov's modified Grothendieck polynomials and can be thought of as an equivariant K-theoretic version of Postnikov's toric Schur function. We also provide new polynomial representatives for equivariant K-theory classes of Richardson varieties and their variants.
item.dc:creator: Vassily Gorbounov, Christian Korff, Leonardo C. Mihalcea

item.title: Ax-Schanuel with derivatives for mixed period mappings
item.description: arXiv:2110.03489v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the Ax-Schanuel property of the derivatives of mixed period mappings. We also prove the jet space reformulation of this result. The proofs use the Ax-Schanuel result for principal bundles with flat connections obtained by Bl\'{a}zquez-Sanz, Casale, Freitag, and Nagloo.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chung Tak Chiu

item.title: Counting stringy points on a family of character varieties
item.description: arXiv:2411.05563v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide explicit formulas for the number of stringy points over finite fields of parabolic type A character varieties with generic semisimple monodromy. This leads to formulas for their stringy E-polynomials. In particular, they satisfy the Betti Topological Mirror Symmetry Conjecture of T. Hausel and M. Thaddeus and a refinement regarding isotypic components. Our proof is based on a Frobenius-type formula for Clifford-type settings and an analysis of it in a specific set-up related to regular wreath products with cyclic groups.
item.dc:creator: Lucas de Amorin, Martin Mereb

item.title: Formal models for relative adic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2507.11073v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend Raynaud's theory of formal models from rigid-analytic spaces over a nonarchimedean field to uniform qcqs adic spaces $X$, with no finite-type assumptions, over an arbitrary Tate affinoid base $S$. The key new ingredient is the notion of a normalized formal blow-up which takes on the role played by admissible formal blow-ups in the classical theory.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Dine

item.title: On The Motivic Leray-Hirsch Theorem For Pure Tate Fibre Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2511.21918v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a Leray-Hirsch theorem for a smooth proper morphism over a smooth integral base whose generic fibre has a pure Tate motive. We further explore and highlight some key applications of this theorem.
item.dc:creator: Esmail Arasteh Rad, Somayeh Habibi

item.title: On the rational points in conics of a cubic surface
item.description: arXiv:2601.10895v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study rational and integral points lying on finite collections of conics on non-ruled cubic surfaces over a number field. We extend the global determinant method to hypersurfaces in linear subvarieties, retaining dependence on the height of their Cayley forms. The universal Deligne pairing identifies the Chow line bundle on a residual conic pencil with three times of the universal bundle. Uniform bounds for cubic curves then control the number of conics of bounded height and give uniform estimates for their contribution to auxiliary coverings.
item.dc:creator: Chunhui Liu

item.title: Linear systems on blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2601.21958v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by various equivalent versions of the SHGH conjecture for $\mathbb P^2$ blown up at very general points, we propose a similar conjecture for Hirzebruch surfaces. We prove that this conjecture is true for the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$ blown up at $r\leqslant e+5$ very general points.
item.dc:creator: Cyril J. Jacob, Ronnie Sebastian

item.title: On Automorphism Groups of (1,2)-Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.25554v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $S$ be a minimal surface of general type with $K_S^2=1$ and $p_g(S)=2$, called a $(1,2)$-surface. We give a geometric recovery and refinement of D. Wen's bound $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200$ using the canonical genus-two fibration and the double-cover model over the Hirzebruch surface $\Sigma_2$. Computing $\mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_2)$ from its Cox ring separates the action on the base $\mathbb{P}^1$ from the vertical kernel. If $\overline K_0$ denotes the vertical image on $\Sigma_2$, then $\overline K_0$ is cyclic of order $5$, $4$, $2$, or $1$, and we prove the respective sharp bounds $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200, 192, 48, 80$. The proof combines singularity indices of genus-two fibrations with invariant divisors arising from the branch equation. We also construct admissible branch divisors attaining all four bounds and show that their full automorphism groups are, respectively, $(C_{10}\times C_{10})\rtimes C_2$, $(BO_{48}\times C_8)/\langle(-I,J^4)\rangle$, $(BT_{24}\times C_4)/\langle(-I,J^2)\rangle$, and $C_{40}\times C_2$. Here $BO_{48}$ and $BT_{24}$ denote the binary octahedral and binary tetrahedral groups, respectively, and $J$ denotes a generator of the corresponding cyclic factor.
item.dc:creator: Hang Zhao

item.title: $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectedness of moduli of vector bundles on a stacky curve
item.description: arXiv:2609.28203v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{C}$ be a projective stacky curve over an infinite field $k$ with the coarse space $C$, a geometrically connected smooth projective curve, together with a generating sheaf $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathfrak{C}$. We consider the moduli stack of $\mathcal{E}$-semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant and multiplicities on $\mathfrak{C}$, and show that it is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected if and only if it admits a $k$-rational point. We show that this holds whenever genus of $C$ is at least $2$ and $C(k)\neq \emptyset$. As a consequence, we conclude that, for any system of weights $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$, the moduli stack of parabolic $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$-semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant and quasi-parabolic data on a geometrically connected smooth projective curve is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected.
item.dc:creator: Sujoy Chakraborty, Saurav Holme Choudhury, Rakesh Pawar

item.title: On the transcendental Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.31089v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture for transcendental K\"ahler classes in the case of trivial automorphisms. Indeed, we show the existence of Special K\"ahler Fujita Approximations of big cohomology classes associated to big test configurations, establishing the equivalence between the uniform $K$-stability and the strengthened version for models. More generally, we show that any big cohomology class on a compact K\"ahler manifold admits such Special K\"ahler Fujita Approximations: the volume and the analogue of the Riemann-Roch coefficient of the big class are both approximated by those of K\"ahler classes on higher compactifications.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Trusiani

item.title: On orbits of the automorphism group of toroidal spherical varieties
item.description: arXiv:2609.35683v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study the orbits of the automorphism group on a toroidal spherical variety. In the affine case, we prove that two points lie in the same orbit of the identity component if and only if the kernels of the homomorphisms from the divisor class group to their local divisor class groups coincide. These kernels are described in terms of $B$-stable prime divisors. For a smooth complete toroidal spherical variety, we obtain a similar criterion using the monoids generated by the classes of $B$-stable prime divisors that do not contain a given $G$-orbit.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Chernov, Klim Rolgin

item.title: Markman--Markushevich principle and Lagrangian fibrations on O'Grady six-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20044v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To any compact holomorphically symplectic manifold and a nef BBF-isotropic class we associate a quasi-projective variety called the Markman--Markushevich space which parametrises the Lagrangian fibrations with this isotropic class modulo Tate--Shafarevich twists. We give a systematic interpretation of known results about Tate--Shafarevich twists of Lagrangian fibrations using this space, employ it to obtain a conjectural result for the last deformation type for which such a result is not yet proposed, and make some first steps towards its proof. As a byproduct, we generalise the results of Kumar on existence Shioda--Inose partners for abelian surfaces to a slightly more general class of K3 surfaces, and associate a canonical K3 surface with transcendental lattice isometric to $U^2\oplus\langle-2\rangle^2$ to a smooth cubic surface with a choice of a Schl\"afli double-six. Finally, we construct a noncompact six-manifold with an abelian fibration associated to a cubic surface with a Schl\"afli double-six, and give its interpretation in terms of the K3 surfaces we introduced.
item.dc:creator: Rodion D\'eev

item.title: Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.28456v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.
item.dc:creator: Jagadish Pine

item.title: The symplectic isotopy problem for rational cuspidal curves
item.description: arXiv:1907.06787v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define a suitably tame class of singular symplectic curves in 4-manifolds, namely those whose singularities are modeled on complex curve singularities. We study the corresponding symplectic isotopy problem, with a focus on rational curves with irreducible singularities (rational cuspidal curves) in the complex projective plane. We prove that every such curve is isotopic to a complex curve in degrees up to 5, and for curves with one singularity whose link is a torus knot. Classification results of symplectic isotopy classes rely on pseudo-holomorphic curves together with a symplectic version of birational geometry of log pairs and techniques from 4-dimensional topology.
item.dc:creator: Marco Golla, Laura Starkston

item.title: On the Kummer pro-\'etale cohomology of $\mathbb B_{\operatorname{dR}}$
item.description: arXiv:2501.16916v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate $p$-adic cohomologies of log rigid analytic varieties over a $p$-adic field. For a log rigid analytic variety $X$ defined over a discretely valued field, we compute the Kummer pro-\'etale cohomology of $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$ and $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}$. When $X$ is defined over $\mathbb{C}_p$, we introduce a logarithmic ${B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-cohomology theory, serving as a deformation of log de Rham cohomology. Additionally, we establish the log de Rham-\'etale comparison in this setting and prove the degeneration of both the Hodge-Tate and Hodge-log de Rham spectral sequences when $X$ is proper and log smooth.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Shao

item.title: Three-periodic helices on elliptic curves and their associated regular algebras
item.description: arXiv:2604.21900v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $k$ denote an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let $X$ denote a smooth elliptic curve over $k$. Given a three-periodic elliptic helix $\underline{\mathcal{E}}$ of vector bundles over $X$ with endomorphism $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ and quadratic cover $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$, we prove that $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ is the quotient of $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$ by a degree three family of normal elements, generalizing a result of the authors to the case in which $\operatorname{dim }(\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}})_{i, i+1}$ isn't a constant function of $i$. We then show that $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ is noetherian if and only if it has polynomial growth, and in this case, the ranks of any three consecutive bundles in the helix are a Markov triple. Furthermore, in this case $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$ is a noetherian GK-three $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra which is ${\sf Proj }$-equivalent to an elliptic algebra. We conclude the paper by constructing several new families of elliptic helices with exponential growth.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Chan, Adam Nyman

item.title: Unipotent representations and the categorical trace of Frobenius
item.description: arXiv:2609.39721v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a new proof of the classification of unipotent representations for split finite groups of Lie type. To do this, we first construct an (infinity, 2)-categorification of Lusztig's map from the Hecke algebra to the asymptotic algebra. Then we use the theory of weights to show that it induces an isomorphism after applying trace of Frobenius.
item.dc:creator: Wyatt Reeves

item.title: Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits for Positive Factorial Multiples
item.description: arXiv:2610.28338v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\tau(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values. We show that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, some positive integer $m$ satisfies \[ \tau(mk!)\leq \exp\!\left(O\!\left((\log k)^{2/3}(\log\log k)^{1/3}\right)\right). \] The proof combines unconditional results of Lenstra, Pila and Pomerance on smooth numbers in short intervals and on orders of genus-two Jacobians with a five-parameter family carrying a rational divisor class of infinite order. We encode rational divisor arithmetic, including the tests determining its branches, by a nonzero division-free integer circuit. A common finite sampling space yields circuits whose outputs collectively contain every prime at most $k$, and repeated squaring supplies the required factorial valuations. The circuit bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and GPT-6.1 Sol.
item.dc:creator: Liang Zhang
